exposure: ROTEM parameters (EXTEM clotting time (CT), clot formation time (CFT), alpha angle, A10, A20, maximum clot formation (MCF), maximum lysis)
cohort: The study recruited 92 women aged 18 to 50 years old, at >=34 weeks of gestation, who underwent scheduled cesarean delivery or normal spontaneous vaginal delivery at university-affiliated hospitals.
finding: The ROTEM EXTEM maximum lysis parameter, along with age, blood loss type, delivery mode, and gestational age, had a significant effect on blood loss, with every one-percent increase in maximum lysis associated with a 44-milliliter increase in blood loss.
mod_finding: Cesarean deliveries resulted in 522 more milliliters of blood loss than normal spontaneous vaginal delivery.
